title: Southern Syncopators and Piron's band
summary: He lists the members of the Southern Syncopators and explains Piron's use of them; Piron's older six-piece band was giving way to bigger bands.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. Now, uh, who was in this Southern Syncopators? Can you remember, man?

Yeah, in the Southern, uh, Syncopators, there was, uh, Eddie Pearson on trombone, Leo Dejo trumpet, and a trumpet player named DeRuxa, DeRuxa, DeRuxa from over the river. Mm-hmm. And the sax section was, uh, Elliot Taylor. Mm-hmm. Uh, Arthur Durbney, Joe Ruzon. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. And, uh, rhythm section was Sidney Montague, I believe Booker Washington on bass, and Allegretto on piano.

I don't remember them using any bands, you know, it might have been Sidney Fluge, or, no, I don't remember the bands that played that. Well, that's the band that, um, when Peter had the idea of this band, this original band, they used to play, he used to take dates, and, uh, he'd hire this band because at that time there was...

that old band, Pulon band was about, I believe about six pieces or so, and ten, eight and ten piece band were coming, becoming popular then. And then there was the younger musicians, you know, so I remember I was working with Sidney Desby and he had let me go for Randy Hall.
